headline: Your 206 bones are living organs that grow, heal, and constantly rebuild themselves
universal_truth: Structure enables function; the framework determines what's possible
fun_facts: You're born with about 270 bones; many fuse together, leaving adults with 206
Bone is five times stronger than steel of the same weight
Your skeleton is completely replaced every 10 years through constant remodeling
discussion_questions: What structure or framework enables what you do?
How does knowing bones are living and constantly changing affect how you see your skeleton?
What happens when structure fails or changes?

hook.script: You might think of your skeleton as a static scaffold—dead support structure. But your bones are alive. They grow, heal, and completely replace themselves every decade. Your skeleton isn't just structure; it's a living, dynamic system.

cliff.script: Bones seem solid and unchanging, yet they can heal when broken and adapt to stress. How can something so rigid also be so dynamic? What's happening inside bones that we can't see?
cliff.prompt: How do bones heal and change?

options.text: Bones contain living cells that constantly break down and rebuild bone tissue
options.response: Yes. Osteoclasts break down bone; osteoblasts build it. This constant remodeling allows healing and adaptation.

options.text: Bones have a blood supply that delivers healing materials when needed
options.response: Blood supply is essential, but the key is specialized bone cells...

fact1.title: Living Scaffold
fact1.script: Bones contain living cells in a matrix of minerals and collagen. Osteoclasts constantly dissolve old bone while osteoblasts build new bone. Your entire skeleton is replaced roughly every 10 years. You're not the same skeleton you were a decade ago.

fact2.title: Stronger Than Steel
fact2.script: Bone is remarkably strong—weight for weight, it's five times stronger than steel. Yet it's flexible enough not to shatter. This combination of strength and flexibility comes from mixing hard minerals with flexible collagen. Biology outengineers engineering.

fact3.title: Bones Fuse
fact3.script: Babies have about 270 bones. By adulthood, many have fused, leaving 206. Your skull started as multiple plates that could shift during birth, then fused. Bones aren't static—they develop and merge throughout life.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Structure enables function. Your skeleton reminds us that what seems like passive framework is actually actively supporting everything else. Tend to your structures—they make everything else possible.

outro.script: That's Day 89. Tomorrow—Day 90—we'll explore what love does to us. Until then, appreciate the living framework that holds you together.

growTrack.title: Structure Audit - What Frameworks Support You?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify and strengthen supporting structures in life
growTrack.activity: Like bones support your body, what structures support your life—routines, relationships, principles? Identify one 'skeletal' structure that's essential to your functioning. Is it healthy? Does it need strengthening?
